accounting.rationale: Both sentences belong to this constraint: module-specification placement and the per-module at-most-one limit for omitted-list access statements. Other PRIVATE productions are not counted as access-stmt occurrences.

The complete PDF134 paragraph distinguishes listed non-module identifiers from omitted-list defaults, unlisted import providers and locally declared identifiers, including a locally extended imported generic. It then gives PUBLIC, PRIVATE and absent-statement default cases. The new requirements describe the defining statement mechanisms; S8.5.2-001/-002/-003 retain their existing declaration/default/use-access interpretations and metadata. Three existing binding links cite this base unit; newly supplied accounting/source review context must stale them honestly, not rewrite their bases.

The section continues on PDF135. The all-provider policy rule requires use association, no local declaration and every relevant provider name in a local access statement. All PRIVATE and any PUBLIC are alternatives inside that complete premise, not a universal any-public-use-path rule.

The first original note is a module prefix illustrating an omitted-list PRIVATE default and one PUBLIC list with names, defined assignment and an operator. It is not a complete ready-to-run program or a new normative requirement.
MODULE EX supplies the appropriate general context but does not stand for a component or binding definition.
This is an access-stmt with no list, not a statement assigning PRIVATE explicitly to every entity and not R745 or R747.
The separate PUBLIC list names three individual access identifiers; their entities must be validly declared in a completed example.
ASSIGNMENT(=) is a generic-spec, not an ordinary access-name or an instruction to make every intrinsic assignment a procedure.
OPERATOR(+) illustrates the other generic-spec route. Its actual defined-operation interfaces must satisfy15.4.3.4.2; PRIVATE does not make a valid intrinsic fallback an error.
Entity definitions, complete generic specifics and END MODULE are required before proposing a fixture. The fragment is not copied into a no-op classifier or counted as execution evidence.

The second note illustrates a provider-specific PRIVATE policy, an explicitly PUBLIC imported type identifier, and independently default-public local procedures. The example does not change the provider's own accessibility.
m2 is the policy-setting/exporting module. It is distinct from the used provider m1.
USE m1 supplies the direct same-scope reference required by C875; a complete future context must supply m1's public definitions first.
PRIVATE m1 is a listed module-name policy for imports. It is not a no-list PRIVATE statement or an accessibility attribute assigned to the module entity.
PUBLIC m_type explicitly exposes that receiving identifier despite its provider-specific private default. It does not expose every other import or alter component/binding accessibility.
Locally declared entities follow local defaults, not the module-name policy applied to imports; legitimate generic merging is a separate qualified local-declaration case.
No no-list PRIVATE statement is shown, so the illustrated local procedure identifiers retain the ordinary public default rather than inheriting PRIVATE m1.
The ellipsis is explanatory. No unavailable provider, undefined type, missing procedure body, new case, link or coverage is supplied by this note.

requirements.title: An access statement has a qualified optional identifier list
requirements.definition: An access statement uses an access-spec and may have an access-id list. The double-colon separator is optional within the list-bearing form; it is not a standalone alternative when the list is absent. R807 owns PUBLIC/PRIVATE and R401 supplies the nonempty comma-list convention. C873 and the other access-identifier constraints retain their own premises.

The forms are admitted without an identifier list; default interpretation is S8.6.1-002. These grammar controls are not no-op supplementary effect programs.
pending.colon-without-list-exclusion: PENDING complete module contexts with PUBLIC :: and separately PRIVATE :: but no following access-id list, repaired only by deleting the separator. Preserve the surrounding module and declarations. Every list element must be legal under R831/C874-C876. The spelling alone does not prove per-element semantics; keep the module-name policy separate from explicit entity accessibility.

A component designator, array element or type-bound binding name is not silently substituted for a module-level identifier of the required category.

Do not create a second empty program for a spelling already owned by a qualified R830/C874 case or treat a bare intrinsic-type keyword as an ineligible entity without name resolution.

Supply complete module procedures with12.6.4.8.2's dtv/unit/iostat/iomsg and formatted iotype/v_list characteristics, correct dtv intent and CLASS for an extensible type. requirements.title: Access statements belong in module specifications with at most one omitted-list statement
requirements.definition: An access-stmt occurs only in a module specification-part, which contains at most one access-stmt without an access-id list. The limit is on this statement category, not all PUBLIC/PRIVATE spellings or all statements in a file. Multiple lawful listed statements remain subject to their separate identifier and attribute rules.

Add a used-provider module-name policy only with complete C875/C876 context. requirements.title: Every access-name has one of six specified entity roles
requirements.definition: Each access-name names a module, variable, procedure, nonintrinsic type, named constant or namelist group. The generic-spec alternative is separately defined by R831. The parsed entity role, namespace and scope matter; word spelling alone does not identify an intrinsic type, common block, component or procedure.

pending.used-module-name: PENDING a complete acyclic provider/receiver module pair with the provider defined first, USE provider in the receiver, and one PUBLIC or PRIVATE provider entry. It is a module-origin default policy, not an attribute assigned to the module entity. Distinct module and local entity names avoid unrelated global/local identifier collisions.
pending.variable-name: PENDING qualified compile controls naming separately declared ordinary INTEGER scalar and array module variables in access statements. No data is read before definition, and declaration access-specs are not repeated. Semantic import/export effects require a separate actual consumer, not a no-op supplementary classifier.
pending.procedure-name: PENDING a fully defined scalar module function and a separately qualified external-procedure declaration with a complete matching definition and correct EXTERNAL, type and explicit-interface premises where required. PUBLIC/PRIVATE acts on the actual module-level procedure identifier, not its type-bound binding alias. Abstract-interface and generic-name identification must be resolved under their canonical rules before any additional role claim.
pending.nonintrinsic-type-name: PENDING complete derived-type, named enum-type and enumeration-type declarations followed by access statements naming their type identifiers. Keep R760 versus R767 forms, prior definitions and their own accessibility/constructor rules; do not append an access-spec to grammar that does not allow it. Compile controls do not prove type-member access, C representation or an enumeration value oracle.
pending.named-constant-name: PENDING a complete module with an explicitly defined INTEGER PARAMETER and one named accessibility specification, plus a separately source-qualified enumerator relation under7.6.1. Retain each constant's defining owner and do not derive integer kinds or representation assumptions from its accessibility.
pending.namelist-group-name: PENDING a complete module declaring INTEGER objects and NAMELIST /settings/ object, with an access statement naming settings. Distinguish the group from its member objects and from a COMMON block name. Any future I/O observation must define the objects and supply a real independent I/O oracle; declaration admission alone is a compile/positive-control.
pending.other-name-class-gates: PENDING exact19.2/19.3 classification before any ineligible-name negative. COMMON names are not added to C874's list;19.3.2 can make a common-block homonym in an access statement denote a local identifier instead. Components/bindings have their own type scopes, and spelling an intrinsic keyword does not prove an intrinsic-type entity because names are context dependent.14.2.2 separately lists abstract interfaces as use-accessible entities: resolve their actual naming role before asserting either a C874 rejection or admission. A causal complete negative and minimal role-valid repair are required; unknown-name or implicit-typing errors cannot be substituted.

requirements.oracle: Finite complete contexts for the six literal source categories and explicitly held namespace/classification contrasts. A source-qualified canonical role or grammar relation precedes any negative; no invented third-party module or undeclared-name report is evidence.
requirements.oracle_limitation: All seven facets are pending. C874's list is not replaced by a broad use-association entity list or by generic-spec syntax. requirements.title: A named provider module requires a USE reference in the containing scope
requirements.definition: A module named in an access statement is referenced by a USE statement in the same scoping unit as that access statement. A reference elsewhere in the source file or only along an indirect import path is not this local USE. Module-name classification and the normal acyclic/available-provider USE conditions remain necessary.

pending.same-scope-use-required: PENDING a complete provider module and a receiver naming that distinct provider in an access statement but lacking a local USE, repaired only by inserting a valid USE provider before IMPLICIT NONE. The provider's definitions and source/build order must be supplied, with no local homonym. First establish that the subject resolves as the module and qualify the missing same-scope USE cause; an unknown variable, missing module artifact or unsupported module-name policy is not credit. A self-reference is not a valid repair.
pending.only-renaming-references: PENDING complete controls for USE provider without ONLY, with an empty ONLY list, and with ONLY/renaming of a public entity, each accompanied by one provider module-name access entry. All are references to that provider under14.2.2p1. Policy applies to actual accessed identifiers; it neither imports omitted names nor turns the local renamed variable into a module name.
pending.nested-and-indirect-use-gates: PENDING complete sources where USE provider appears only in a contained procedure, another program unit, or a re-exporting intermediate module while the receiver's own access statement names provider. Repair by adding the receiver's direct USE, preserving the existing acyclic graph and full definitions.3.120 excludes nested scoping units from the enclosing scope; the immediate used providers, not merely the ultimate origin, must be identified before reporting or default resolution.

The entire module-name/access-statement/local-USE relation and legitimate source origins must be calibrated later. Source ambiguity, unresolved interfaces, unsupported facilities, echoes and compiler failures remain explicit noncredit gates.

requirements.title: Each provider module name occurs at most once in a module's access statements
requirements.definition: Within one receiving module, a module name occurs at most once across all access statements. The quantifier includes repeated entries in one list and repetitions across statements, regardless of equal or different access-specs. It is not a limit on the number of USE statements or on a different receiving module's independent policy.

pending.duplicate-module-in-one-list: PENDING a complete provider and receiver with a valid local USE and PUBLIC :: provider, provider, with PRIVATE as a separate variant. Remove only the second module-name entry and comma for the control. Require the repeated module-name access-policy cause, not an ordinary entity's repeated accessibility attribute or a missing USE.
pending.repeated-module-across-statements: PENDING validly supplied provider/receiver contexts with two PUBLIC provider statements and separately two PRIVATE provider statements. Delete only the second statement. The same module entity and local USE remain fixed; C875 and R830/R831 remain satisfied in both sources.
pending.mixed-policy-repetition: PENDING PUBLIC provider followed by PRIVATE provider, and the reverse order, in otherwise identical complete contexts. Removing only the second statement is the repair. Different policies do not permit a last-wins update, and the generic word accessibility without the actual module-name repetition relation is not a sufficient diagnostic oracle.

Keep provider and imported-variable names distinct.

requirements.oracle_limitation: No compiler probe or diagnostic predicate is authored. Future evidence must preserve complete case bytes, exact causes and live origins, including distinct legitimate statement spans if required by the reporting processor. No source-line coalescing, broadened span, forced fatal rejection or unsupported/ICE/recovery credit.

requirements.title: Listed non-module identifiers receive the statement's explicit accessibility
requirements.source: 8.6.1 p1 first sentence, physical PDF134, printed120
requirements.definition: An access statement with a list explicitly assigns its PUBLIC or PRIVATE accessibility to each listed access-id that is not a module name. Module-name entries select import defaults instead. Accessibility is via the relevant identifier, not an unconditional entity-wide change across aliases, use paths, component names, bindings or a specific implementation name.

pending.listed-individual-identifiers: PENDING complete provider/consumer parents with one PUBLIC named constant or module function in a PRIVATE-default provider and the reciprocal PRIVATE identifier in a PUBLIC-default provider. The module entry sets the imported token's default while the non-module entry explicitly sets local_token. A consumer must use the actual identifiers and require literal17/23 with completion events. An unrelated local identifier retains the local default; any rejection proof for it is a separate canonical C1409 relation.

Specify one alias PUBLIC and the other PRIVATE once each; observe the public alias's actual literal value, and qualify any private alias ONLY-import contrast under C1409.14.2.2p7-p9 determines the identifiers. A real consumer invokes g on a defined literal input and checks the independent result and call/completion events. This is not a type-bound generic USE test or proof that a legal intrinsic fallback must fail.

Type-name access is independent of components, bindings and implementation names; inherited inaccessible members stay inaccessible, public overrides cannot become private, and shared generic/type names retain C7107/C7108 resolution. Preserve original runtime-effect versus run/positive-control roles and all existing link anchors. No new execution, automatic link or promotion is approved.

S8.5.2 retains its declaration/default/use-access requirements; related canonical observations are candidates, not duplicate local fixture slots.

requirements.title: Statement defaults are selected by local declaration and the complete set of used providers
requirements.source: 8.6.1 p1 default clauses and p2, physical PDF134-135, printed120-121
requirements.definition: A no-list access statement specifies the module default for locally declared entity identifiers and identifiers imported from a module whose name is absent from all local access statements. PUBLIC selects a public default, PRIVATE a private default, and no such statement leaves a public default. An identifier both imported and locally declared follows the local-declaration default. For a use-associated identifier not locally declared, when every module from which it is accessed is named in a local access statement, all PRIVATE specifications give a private default and any PUBLIC specification gives a public default. This computes defaults; it does not override an explicit individual access specification or make a private provider identifier importable.

pending.local-default-forms: PENDING one finite canonical provider/consumer family with a locally declared named constant17 and module procedure returning23, under absent, one PUBLIC, or one PRIVATE no-list statement. Public cases require actual imported values and exact completion, not empty modules. Private ONLY-import diagnostics and their sole default-keyword repairs retain C1409. These are the defining statement/default-selection premises consumed by S8.5.2-002; reuse a reviewed family rather than duplicate its existing plans.
pending.unlisted-provider-fallback: PENDING a complete provider exporting token=17 and a receiving module USEing it but never naming that provider in an access statement. Exercise the receiver's absent/PUBLIC/PRIVATE no-list forms with no explicit token access specification or local redeclaration. The imported identifier follows this ordinary default route; provider PUBLIC is necessary for the initial import but does not force onward PUBLIC.
pending.single-provider-policy: PENDING paired full source graphs with PRIVATE provider in an otherwise PUBLIC-default receiver and PUBLIC provider in an otherwise PRIVATE-default receiver, following local USE provider. The solely imported token takes the provider-specific default, while independent local declarations take the local default. Use actual re-export/consumer observations or source-qualified C1409 pairs, not an attribute assigned to the module entity.
pending.all-private-providers: PENDING a root constant token=17 re-exported through two modules, both USEd under the same identifier in the receiver, so there is one ultimate entity rather than two ambiguous variables. Name every used provider in PRIVATE access statements, leave token nonlocal and without explicit access, and require a PRIVATE default even with local PUBLIC default. A focused future C1409 repair changes only one provider policy to PUBLIC; full source/build ordering and exact unavailable identifier cause are prerequisites.
pending.any-public-provider: PENDING the same two-provider same-ultimate-entity graph with PUBLIC/PUBLIC, PUBLIC/PRIVATE and PRIVATE/PUBLIC policies under a local PRIVATE default. Every relevant provider is listed and the identifier is not locally declared. Real conforming consumer runs require imported17 and independent completion events; varying statement order must not create last-wins semantics. No duplicate canonical re-export executions are created here.
pending.incomplete-provider-policies: PENDING the same two-provider graph with one provider unlisted. A listed PUBLIC policy plus local PRIVATE default does not satisfy p2's every-provider premise; the unlisted-provider route selects PRIVATE. Conversely a listed PRIVATE policy with local PUBLIC default selects PUBLIC via that route. Keep the identifier nonlocal and without explicit access, and hold all provider/ultimate-entity relationships fixed. Do not generalize any PUBLIC path beyond the complete p2 premise.
pending.imported-plus-local-generic: PENDING a legitimate imported generic also declared by a local interface extension, not an illegal redeclaration of an imported variable. Use distinct fully defined scalar INTEGER-argument and scalar LOGICAL-argument specific functions, both with fixed INTEGER results, under C1514. Give the provider a PUBLIC policy but the receiver a PRIVATE local default: the locally extended generic follows the local default. A one-default-keyword PUBLIC repair admits actual calls to both specifics with independent literal results17/23 and visit/return completion. Result type alone is not generic distinguishability.
pending.explicit-access-and-origin-boundaries: PENDING finite canonical relations showing an explicit individual PUBLIC/PRIVATE specification taking precedence over the computed default, separate local aliases of one ultimate entity, repeated USEs of one provider, and immediate used-provider names versus the ultimate origin. A policy for an indirectly reached root still needs C875's direct local USE if that root is named. Component/binding PRIVATE productions never select this module default. All8.5.2 and existing canonical-link owners, inputs and roles remain unchanged.

requirements.oracle: A finite complete source-provenance and local-declaration matrix with real providers, lawful generic merges, independent literal data/dispatch results and exact completion events where runtime effects are observed. S8.5.2-002 consumes these statement-defined defaults; overlapping source obligations must share independently reviewed canonical evidence rather than copied fixtures or reciprocal owner rewrites.
requirements.oracle_limitation: Every facet is pending. This is not a compiler-consensus or text-classifier oracle. Incomplete origin policies, a locally declared generic, two distinct ambiguous ultimate variables, a private exporting identifier and a missing module are different conditions. Pure default prose does not mandate rejection; any negative keeps its actual numbered/name-scope basis, minimally repaired control and precise live-origin cause. Required runtime semantics are not downgraded to compile-only for unsupported module-name policies.
